title: CUBE
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server CUBE operator to generate multiple grouping sets in a single query.

data.text: The CUBE operator is a subclause of the GROUP BY clause that generates all possible grouping sets from the specified dimension columns. It is useful for creating multi-dimensional summary reports.

A grouping set defines a group of columns by which you group data. A single query with an aggregate function typically defines one grouping set. CUBE extends this by generating multiple grouping sets automatically.

data.title: Single Grouping Set
data.content: A basic query with one grouping set by brand.
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    SUM(sales)
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    brand;

data.title: CUBE Syntax
data.content: Generates all possible grouping sets from the dimension columns.
data.code:
SELECT
    d1,
    d2,
    d3,
    aggregate_function(c4)
FROM
    table_name
GROUP BY
    CUBE(d1, d2, d3);

data.text: For N dimension columns, CUBE generates 2^N grouping sets. This includes all combinations of the columns, from the full set down to the empty set.
The following query uses CUBE with two dimension columns, brand and category, producing four grouping sets.

data.title: CUBE with Two Columns
data.content: Generates grouping sets for brand and category combinations.
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    CUBE(brand, category);

data.alt: SQL Server CUBE example output showing four grouping sets

data.text: The four grouping sets produced are: (brand, category), (brand), (category), and the empty set () which returns the grand total.
You can reduce the number of grouping sets by using CUBE partially. When CUBE is applied to only some of the columns, it generates fewer grouping sets.

data.title: Partial CUBE
data.content: Uses CUBE on category only, with brand as a regular grouping column.
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    brand,
    CUBE(category);

data.alt: SQL Server partial CUBE example output

data.title: CUBE Key Points
points: CUBE generates all possible grouping sets from the specified dimension columns.
For N columns, CUBE produces 2^N grouping sets.
Use partial CUBE to reduce the number of grouping sets when not all combinations are needed.
CUBE is a subclause of the GROUP BY clause.
